title: SharePoint admin center: Data access governance report of sites a group can access
notes: claim 64: severity blocker on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
the verifier wrote "hold" but listed no blocker and fewer than three majors; the claims decide, so the page is not held
summary: The report's scope, licensing, controls and rollout dates are supported. However, the impact rationale promises that site owners and group members see no change, although Microsoft has not stated the arrival default; that assurance needs to be narrowed.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a new SharePoint admin report showing every site a group can access and the extent of access.
claims.quote: With this new report, SharePoint admins can now see every site a group can access and the extent of that access.

claims.claim: Broad-membership groups and groups for vendors can expose sensitive content to unintended recipients.
claims.quote: A single group with broad membership or a special group for vendors etc. - can expose sensitive content to unintended recipients.

claims.claim: Group reports exclude access inherited through nested-group membership.
claims.quote: Group reports don't expand nested-group permissions. If a security group is a member of another group, access granted to the parent group isn't included in the nested group's report.

claims.claim: A ZIP download can contain CSV files for all groups included in a report.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity PermissionsReport -ReportType Snapshot -Workload SharePoint -Name <name> -TargetGroups <groups> generates the group report.
claims.quote:
Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight `
    -ReportEntity PermissionsReport `
    -ReportType Snapshot `
    -Workload SharePoint `
    -Name "GroupPermissionsReport" `
    -TargetGroups $groups

claims.claim: TargetGroups takes the group objects returned by Get-MgGroup.
claims.quote: Retrieve the groups with Get-MgGroup, then pass the returned group objects directly to the TargetGroups parameter.

claims.claim: The Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight reference currently omits TargetGroups, unlike the guide.
claims.quote: Searched: TargetGroups in the complete fetched Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight reference; no match in its syntax or parameter list. Read the PowerShell guide's Generate a group permission state report section, which documents -TargetGroups.

claims.claim: Data access governance reports are accessed at SharePoint admin center > Reports > Data access governance.
claims.quote: Sign in to the SharePoint admin center ... In the left pane, expand Reports and then select Data access governance.

claims.claim: Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity <entity> lists Data access governance reports.
claims.quote:
Lists various 'Data Access Governance' (DAG) reports in SharePoint admin center. ... Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight
    -ReportEntity <ReportEntityEnum>

claims.claim: The PowerShell guide documents Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity PermissionsReport for reviewing user and group report results.
claims.quote:
Use the following command to check user and group permission reports:

Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity PermissionsReport

claims.claim: Microsoft does not describe automatic changes to existing site or group permissions when this report arrives.

claims.fix: Replace the impact rationale with: "Low. Microsoft's notice names SharePoint administrators as the people affected; no source says existing site permissions change on arrival." This preserves the documented audience without asserting an arrival default.
